expect: False premise: the 10% Mn sample delivered more (212 vs 164 mAh/g); the 50% Mn sample released less heat (485.7 vs 901.4 J/g) (p4.L15-21). The paper's own sentence says the lower-Mn sample generated less heat, which its numbers contradict
question: Since the 50% Mn-doped LNO delivered more capacity than the 10% Mn sample, how much more heat did it release in the thermal tests?
rendered:
According to the text, the 50% Mn-doped LNO sample released 485.7 J/g in the thermal tests, and the 10% Mn sample released 901.4 J/g. To find out how much more heat the 50% Mn-doped LNO sample released, we need to subtract the heat released by the 50% Mn-doped LNO sample from the heat released by the 10% Mn sample.

901.4 J/g (10% Mn sample) - 485.7 J/g (50% Mn-doped LNO sample) = 415.7 J/g

So, the 50% Mn-doped LNO sample released 415.7 J/g less heat than the 10% Mn sample in the thermal tests.
